Task instruction: Lift the kitchenpot with two side handles with both arms

Task description: The target is the lidded pot at the center of the table with a handle on each side. Use both arms to grasp the handles and lift the pot as a whole, keeping it roughly upright.

Success criteria: The left and right grippers are each close to the grip area of the corresponding left and right handles of the pot. Both arms lift the pot clearly off the table and hold it suspended; the pot opening faces up, and the body is not noticeably tilted.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping the straight outer sections of the two handles, away from the pot body. Choose straight segments far from corners and joints that can accommodate the finger pads, reducing the risk of touching the pot wall or slipping off a bend.
- Open slightly wider than the grasped rod's thickness and use the handle gap to place fingers on opposite sides. Confirm actual enclosure before closing, avoiding an empty grasp based only on image overlap.
- During two-arm lifting, keep both handles at similar heights and stable relative spacing. Avoid lifting one side first or pulling outward and tilting the pot. If regrasping is needed, restore table support first.
